answer: QC-07: ask the night librarian for Folio 1870-Q, not 1870-R

methods.name: A. classical brute force over keys
methods.notes: decrypt with every key and test the QC-07 prefix; 2^n cost, never touches U

methods.name: B. classical angle scan vs matrix of U
methods.notes: reads U and the eigenstate as numbers (forbidden for the tier); a direct eigenvalue read is O(1) and would be the real shortcut

methods.name: C. repeated Hadamard test (1 use of U per shot)
methods.notes: rms error ~ 2245/sqrt(N) grid steps; need ~1.3e+08 shots per readout for 99% exact; success_rate measured at 10^6 shots

methods.name: D. textbook QPE, 14 counting qubits + inverse QFT
methods.notes: oracle_calls = physical U applications per shot (sum of 2^j); here U^(2^j) is built from the matrix as one gate each (14 gates)

methods.name: D. textbook QPE, t=4 (too few bits)
methods.notes: success_rate is for the exact 14-bit key; the top 4 bits come out right with P=0.99

methods.name: D. textbook QPE, t=8 (too few bits)
methods.notes: success_rate is for the exact 14-bit key; the top 8 bits come out right with P=0.96

methods.name: D. textbook QPE, t=12 (too few bits)
methods.notes: success_rate is for the exact 14-bit key; the top 12 bits come out right with P=0.80

methods.name: E. iterative (semiclassical) QPE, 2 qubits [submitted]
methods.notes: 14 circuits, 1 shot each is enough; checker reports 2q=2, depth 11, 16 gates, 2 active qubits
